https://businesspost.ng/general/illegal-.body: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has arrested 15 suspects, comprising 14 Chinese and one Nigerian, at four illegal lithium processing plants in the Ogere area of Ogun State. The commission disclosed this in a post on its official X account, stating that operatives of its Lagos Zonal Directorate 2 carried out the arrests on Friday, October 23, 2026, following credible intelligence and surveillance. Items recovered during the operation included bags of lithium rocks, 18 mobile devices, four computer laptops, two decoders, a television remote control and a trailer truck. The EFCC said the recovered items had been taken as part of its investigation into the activities of the facilities, adding that the suspects would be charged to court upon the conclusion of investigations. However, the agency did not disclose the specific offences the suspects were alleged to have committed or the ownership of the processing plants. Lithium has become a highly sought-after mineral globally because of its critical role in manufacturing rechargeable batteries used in electric vehicles, smartphones, laptops and renewable energy storage systems. Growing demand for electric vehicles and clean energy technologies has intensified the race to secure lithium supplies, making the mineral increasingly valuable and creating incentives for illegal mining and processing. Nigeria is emerging as a new source of lithium in Africa as the world’s largest producers, like Australia and Chile, are unable to fulfil the growing demand worldwide. However, illegal activities thrive in Nigeria’s extractive sector, denying the government due revenues of up to $9 billion, according to the Nigeria Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (NEITI). The country’s lithium deposits have attracted growing interest from local and foreign operators, while concerns over unregulated extraction, revenue losses, environmental degradation, and the potential circumvention of mining regulations have heightened calls for stricter enforcement. https://businesspost.ng/general/illegal-.title_zh: 非法锂矿开采：经济和金融犯罪委员会在奥贡州拘捕14名中国人和1名尼日利亚人
https://businesspost.ng/general/illegal-.body_zh: 经济和金融犯罪委员会（EFCC）在奥贡州奥盖雷地区的4家非法锂加工厂逮捕了15名嫌疑人，其中14名为中国人、1名为尼日利亚人。该委员会在其官方X账号发布的一则消息中披露，拉各斯第2区分局行动人员于2026年10月23日星期五根据可靠情报和监视行动实施了逮捕。行动中缴获的物品包括装在袋中的锂矿石、18部移动设备、4台笔记本电脑、2个解码器、1个电视遥控器和1辆拖挂卡车。EFCC表示，缴获的物品已作为调查这些工厂经营活动的一部分被查扣，并称调查结束后将把嫌疑人移交法院起诉。然而，该机构没有披露嫌疑人被指控实施的具体罪行，也没有披露这些加工厂的归属。锂已成为全球备受追捧的矿产，因为它在制造用于电动汽车、智能手机、笔记本电脑和可再生能源储存系统的可充电电池方面发挥着关键作用。电动汽车和清洁能源技术需求不断增长，加剧了各国争夺锂供应的竞争，使这种矿产的价值日益提高，也刺激了非法采矿和加工活动。随着澳大利亚和智利等全球最大生产国无法满足全球不断增长的需求，尼日利亚正成为非洲新的锂来源。然而，尼日利亚采掘业的非法活动十分猖獗，使政府损失最高达90亿美元的收入，据尼日利亚采掘业透明度倡议（NEITI）称。该国的锂矿藏吸引了越来越多的本地和外国运营商关注，同时，对不受监管的开采、收入流失、环境破坏以及规避采矿法规的担忧，也强化了要求加强执法的呼声。Adedapo Adesanya是一名记者、多才多艺的学者，也是艺术各个领域的行家。不写作时，他不是埋首阅读自己收藏夹中的众多书籍或文章之一，就是拿着一瓶啤酒或葡萄酒聆听好音乐。他支持世界上最伟大的俱乐部——Manchester United F.C.

https://x.com/annamalindoguy/status/2116.title: REAPER DRONES IN PALAWAN: IS THE PHILIPPINES BECOMING AMERICA’S FORWARD MILITARY OUTPOST?
https://x.com/annamalindoguy/status/2116.snippet:
REAPER DRONES IN PALAWAN: IS THE PHILIPPINES BECOMING AMERICA’S FORWARD MILITARY OUTPOST?

The reported deployment of American MQ-9A Reaper drones to Antonio Bautista Air Base in Puerto Princesa, Palawan, raises a consequential geopolitical question: Is the Philippines strengthening its national defense, or progressively transforming itself into a forward operating platform for American military operations against China?

According to an October 28, 2026, USNI News report, the US Marine Corps’ Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Squadron 1 (VMU-1) is operating Reaper drones from Palawan, placing sophisticated American intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities closer to the disputed Spratly Islands.

This is not the first American Reaper deployment in the Philippines. Similar operations have previously been conducted from Basa Air Base in Pampanga. What makes Palawan strategically significant is its geographical proximity to sensitive South China Sea flashpoints, particularly Ayungin Shoal.

Geography, in geopolitics, is never incidental.

Is Philippine territory increasingly being integrated into America’s military containment strategy against China??

For Manila, the implications are considerably more complicated.

First, the deployment potentially transforms Philippine territory into a more consequential node in the US military’s regional surveillance network. While enhanced intelligence capabilities may strengthen Philippine maritime domain awareness, they also increase the country’s exposure to geopolitical retaliation and military escalation.

Second, the deployment raises fundamental questions about operational sovereignty. Who determines the drones’ missions? Who controls the intelligence collected? Who authorizes surveillance activities? Can Manila veto operations that compromise Philippine national interests?

These questions matter because hosting foreign military capabilities is not synonymous with controlling their strategic consequences.

Third, Palawan’s increasing military significance creates potential vulnerabilities. In a hypothetical US-China confrontation, facilities supporting American military operations could become strategically relevant targets. The Philippines could consequently face risks arising from decisions made beyond its direct control.

Fourth, this development further complicates already deteriorating Philippines-China relations. Beijing may perceive the deployment not merely as defensive surveillance but as evidence of expanding American military encirclement. Such perceptions could intensify countermeasures, accelerate militarization, and narrow diplomatic space. Strengthening national defense should not come at the expense of strategic autonomy.

The Marcos administration must therefore explain the deployment’s operational parameters, intelligence-sharing arrangements, and safeguards against unauthorized military activities.

The Philippines must distinguish between being an American ally and becoming an American frontline. The two are not necessarily the same.

Ultimately, the strategic question is not whether American Reapers can monitor Chinese vessels from Palawan. They can.

The more consequential question is whether Manila controls the risks associated with their presence.

Because when great powers confront each other, geography determines exposure, but political decisions determine vulnerability.

And the Philippines cannot afford to become the battlefield of a confrontation it neither initiated nor controls.

https://x.com/annamalindoguy/status/2116.title_zh: “死神”无人机部署于巴拉望：菲律宾是否正在成为美国的前沿军事据点？
https://x.com/annamalindoguy/status/2116.snippet_zh:
巴洛克无人机部署巴拉望：菲律宾是否正在成为美国的前沿军事据点？

据报道，美国将MQ-9A“死神”无人机部署至位于巴拉望省普林塞萨港的安东尼奥·包蒂斯塔空军基地，这引发了一个影响深远的地缘政治问题：菲律宾是在加强国防，还是正逐步转变为美军针对中国开展行动的前沿作战平台？

据美国海军研究所新闻网站2026年10月28日报道，美国海军陆战队无人航空飞行中队1（VMU-1）正在巴拉望省操作“死神”无人机，使美国先进的情报、监视和侦察能力更接近存在争议的南沙群岛。

这并非美国首次在菲律宾部署“死神”无人机。此前也曾从邦板牙省巴萨空军基地开展类似行动。巴拉望省具有重要战略意义，在于其地理位置靠近南海敏感热点，尤其是仁爱礁。

在地缘政治中，地理位置从来都不是无关紧要的因素。

菲律宾领土是否正日益被纳入美国针对中国的军事遏制战略？

对马尼拉而言，这一问题的影响要复杂得多。

首先，此次部署可能使菲律宾领土成为美军区域监视网络中一个更加重要的节点。情报能力的增强固然可能提升菲律宾对海上领域的态势感知，但也会增加该国遭遇地缘政治报复和军事升级的风险。

其次，此次部署引出了有关行动主权的根本性问题。无人机的任务由谁决定？所收集的情报由谁掌控？监视行动由谁批准？马尼拉能否否决损害菲律宾国家利益的行动？

这些问题之所以重要，是因为接纳外国军事能力并不等于能够控制其战略后果。

第三，巴拉望省军事重要性的提升也会带来潜在脆弱性。在美中发生对抗的假设情境下，支援美军行动的相关设施可能成为具有战略价值的目标。因此，菲律宾可能因自身无法直接控制的决策而面临风险。

第四，这一发展进一步加剧了已经恶化的中菲关系。北京可能将此次部署视为美国扩大军事包围的证据，而不仅仅是一次防御性监视。此类认知可能促使采取反制措施、加快军事化，并压缩外交空间。加强国防不应以牺牲战略自主为代价。

因此，马科斯政府必须说明此次部署的行动参数、情报共享安排，以及防止未经授权军事活动的保障措施。

菲律宾必须区分成为美国盟友与沦为美国前线的差别。两者未必是一回事。

归根结底，真正的战略问题不是美军“死神”无人机能否从巴拉望省监视中国船只。它们能够做到。

更为关键的问题是，马尼拉能否控制这些无人机部署所带来的相关风险。

因为，当大国相互对抗时，地理位置决定暴露程度，而政治决策决定脆弱程度。

菲律宾不能承受成为一场既非自己挑起、也无法自行控制的对抗的战场。

这并非美国首次在菲律宾部署“死神”无人机。此前也曾从邦板牙省巴萨空军基地开展类似行动。巴拉望省具有重要战略意义，在于其地理位置靠近南海敏感热点，尤其是仁爱礁。

在地缘政治中，地理位置从来都不是无关紧要的因素。

菲律宾领土是否正日益被纳入美国针对中国的军事遏制战略？

对马尼拉而言，这一问题的影响要复杂得多。

首先，此次部署可能使菲律宾领土成为美军区域监视网络中一个更加重要的节点。情报能力的增强固然可能提升菲律宾对海上领域的态势感知，但也会增加该国遭遇地缘政治报复和军事升级的风险。

其次，此次部署引出了有关行动主权的根本性问题。无人机的任务由谁决定？所收集的情报由谁掌控？监视行动由谁批准？马尼拉能否否决损害菲律宾国家利益的行动？

这些问题之所以重要，是因为接纳外国军事能力并不等于能够控制其战略后果。

第三，巴拉望省军事重要性的提升也会带来潜在脆弱性。在美中发生对抗的假设情境下，支援美军行动的相关设施可能成为具有战略价值的目标。因此，菲律宾可能因自身无法直接控制的决策而面临风险。

第四，这一发展进一步加剧了已经恶化的中菲关系。北京可能将此次部署视为美国扩大军事包围的证据，而不仅仅是一次防御性监视。此类认知可能促使采取反制措施、加快军事化，并压缩外交空间。加强国防不应以牺牲战略自主为代价。

因此，马科斯政府必须说明此次部署的行动参数、情报共享安排，以及防止未经授权军事活动的保障措施。

菲律宾必须区分成为美国盟友与沦为美国前线的差别。两者未必是一回事。

归根结底，真正的战略问题不是美军“死神”无人机能否从巴拉望省监视中国船只。它们能够做到。

更为关键的问题是，马尼拉能否控制这些无人机部署所带来的相关风险。

因为，当大国相互对抗时，地理位置决定暴露程度，而政治决策决定脆弱程度。

菲律宾不能承受成为一场既非自己挑起、也无法自行控制的对抗的战场。

https://x.com/tribunephl/status/21156445.snippet:
CHINA OWNS 40% OF THE COMPANY RUNNING OUR POWER GRID

The Philippine government owns the country's electricity transmission infrastructure, but the private company operating it, the National Grid Corporation of the Philippines (#NGCP), is 40 percent owned by China's state-owned State Grid Corporation.

That means the Chinese government holds a substantial stake in the company responsible for transmitting electricity across the Philippines, even as tensions between Manila and Beijing persist in the West Philippine Sea.

NGCP maintains that Filipino engineers operate the grid, and there is no established evidence that China possesses a secret mechanism to shut it down.

But the ownership arrangement raises a national security question: Should a foreign government with which the Philippines has an ongoing territorial dispute own part of the company operating its electricity transmission network?

https://x.com/tribunephl/status/21156445.snippet_zh:
运营我国电网的公司40%股权归中国所有

菲律宾政府拥有该国的输电基础设施，但负责运营这些设施的私营公司菲律宾国家电网公司（#NGCP）有40%的股权由中国国有国家电网公司持有。

这意味着，在马尼拉与北京于西菲律宾海持续紧张对峙之际，中国政府仍持有这家负责向菲律宾各地输电的公司相当可观的所有权权益。

NGCP坚持表示，菲律宾工程师负责电网运营，而且没有确凿证据表明中国掌握着秘密手段，可以关闭该电网。

但这种股权安排提出了一个国家安全问题：菲律宾与一个存在持续领土争端的国家，该国政府是否应持有负责运营菲律宾输电网络之公司的部分股权？

https://x.com/amborin/status/21154911112.snippet:
"Russia can technologically help the US build an LNG plant in Alaska...the Polar LNG project worth $25 billion"

"What does Russia need from the US in the Arctic? "two things...first is the market, second is iron. The lifting of sanctions on the Arctic LNG-2 and its LNG carriers will bring back buyers from Japan, India, Southeast Asia and remove the discount that is now being taken away by the only client - China"

"A diesel deal with the United States, an opportunity to expand the supply of Russian fertilizers, and now Russia is offering to work together in the Arctic. How could the Arctic unite Russia and the United States, and what can Moscow offer Washington in return for lifting sanctions on Russian gas?

Russia is working on the possibility of joint work with the United States in the Arctic, Russian President Vladimir Putin said.

"In the Arctic, which I mentioned, we are actively working with many countries of the world and are interested in working together. Quite recently, European partners worked with us in our fields. Now we are working on the possibility of joint work with American partners," Putin said at the summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF).

What kind of joint work with the United States can Russia have?

We are talking about LNG projects. Indeed, after 2022, due to sanctions against Russia, European companies withdrew from participating in gas projects with Russia - in Yamal LNG and Arctic LNG-2. However, cooperation with Chinese companies has reached a new level, says Igor Yushkov, an expert at the National Energy Security Fund (NEF) and the Financial University under the Government of the Russian Federation. There are two Chinese shareholders in the Arctic LNG 2 - CNPC and CNOOC, which were initially afraid of US sanctions against the project and froze their participation. However, Beijing did not change its policy, just the Chinese companies CNPC and CNOOC did not risk access to the dollar, says Mikhail Vakilyan, an expert at the Institute for the Development of Fuel and Energy Technologies.

But after a year and a half, everything changed. In the second half of 2025, China began buying gas from the sanctioned Arctic LNG-2 plant, allocating an entire terminal for the project, and this year opened a second terminal only for Russian LNG. China has even resumed the delivery of modules for the completion of the third stage of the Arctic LNG-2, although earlier deliveries were suspended.

What does Russia need from the United States in the Arctic? "Russia needs two things. The first is the market, the second is iron. The lifting of sanctions on the Arctic LNG-2 and its LNG carriers will bring back buyers from Japan, India, Southeast Asia and remove the discount that is now being taken away by the only client - China. As for iron, the liquefaction compressors at Yamal LNG and Arctic LNG-2 drive the turbines of Baker Hughes, and this is an American company. Service, spare parts and modernization of these cars run into American export bans," says Vakilyan.

"Here is the same scheme as with the diesel deal. We offer the United States mutually beneficial projects and cooperation in the economy in general in exchange for easing anti-Russian sanctions and putting pressure on Ukraine. We show that this cooperation can be very multifaceted and in different areas: diesel, fertilizers, LNG, and so on,"
says the expert of the National Energy Security Fund and the Financial University under the Government of the Russian Federation.

What can Russia offer the United States in the field of LNG in exchange for the lifting of sanctions? Russia can technologically help the United States build an LNG plant in Alaska. We are talking about the Polar LNG project worth $25 billion.

"Novatek has a technological solution for the LNG project in Alaska, which it applied to the Arctic LNG 2. These are reinforced concrete platforms on which liquefaction equipment is poured - and this is, in fact, an LNG plant. Novatek has already built two such platforms with equipment, and has built a center for the construction of large-capacity offshore structures in Belokamenka. The problem is that both this center and the Arctic LNG-2 plant itself fell under US sanctions. Therefore, we can build such a plant in Alaska in exchange for the lifting of sanctions at least from the center for the construction of large-capacity platforms," Yushkov says.

According to him, Russia can pour a platform in this center, build the LNG plant itself on it and only then drive it to Alaska. This is a simpler solution, because it is expensive to build something in the Arctic itself, and creates restrictions on time and the possibility of importing equipment, etc.

"It is not a fact that this story will come to fruition, because there are many sanctions problems and questions about the economics of the project, but nevertheless, the Americans are interested in our technologies for Alaska, and Russia uses and says that it can do it,"
says Yushkov. However, we should not forget that Russia is the main competitor of the United States in terms of gas, and in recent years, the American leadership has consistently squeezed Russian gas out of the European market, the expert adds. And helping LNG from the United States to occupy the market share that the Russian Federation has lost is not a good idea.

However, in addition to the Arctic LNG 2, there is another Russian project that could benefit from cooperation with the United States. This is Yamal LNG, which is not affected by US sanctions. However, the problem is different. From January 1, 2027, the EU bans the supply of any Russian LNG. "In the first half of the year, Europe took almost all of the plant's products - 9.89 million tons. In two months, these volumes need a new route and a new buyer – and an American trader looks natural in this place," says Vakilyan."

https://x.com/amborin/status/21154911112.snippet_zh:
“俄罗斯可以在技术上帮助美国在阿拉斯加建造液化天然气工厂……这就是价值250亿美元的极地LNG项目”

“俄罗斯在北极地区需要美国提供什么？有两样东西……第一是市场，第二是钢铁。取消对Arctic LNG-2及其液化天然气运输船的制裁，将让日本、印度和东南亚的买家回归，并消除目前唯一客户——中国所获得的折扣。至于钢铁，Yamal LNG和Arctic LNG-2的液化压缩机会驱动Baker Hughes的涡轮机，而Baker Hughes是一家美国公司。这些设施的维护、备件供应和现代化改造都受到美国出口禁令的限制。”——瓦基利扬

“俄罗斯与美国达成柴油协议、扩大俄罗斯化肥供应的机会，如今俄罗斯又提出在北极地区合作。北极地区如何促成俄罗斯与美国联手，作为解除对俄罗斯天然气制裁的回报，莫斯科又能向华盛顿提供什么？

俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京表示，俄罗斯正在研究与美国在北极地区合作的可能性。

普京在天然气出口国论坛峰会上说：“在我刚才提到的北极地区，我们正积极与世界上许多国家开展合作，也希望携手合作。就在不久前，欧洲伙伴还曾在我们的油气田与我们合作。现在，我们正在研究与美国伙伴开展合作的可能性。”

俄罗斯可以在哪些方面与美国开展合作？

这涉及液化天然气项目。确实，2022年以后，由于对俄罗斯实施制裁，欧洲企业退出了参与俄罗斯天然气项目，包括Yamal LNG和Arctic LNG-2。然而，俄罗斯联邦政府下属国家能源安全基金和金融大学的专家伊戈尔·尤什科夫表示，与中国企业的合作已经提升到新的水平。Arctic LNG 2有两名中国股东，即CNPC和CNOOC。两家公司最初担心美国会制裁该项目，因而暂停参与。不过，北京并未改变政策，只是中国公司CNPC和CNOOC不愿冒着使用美元结算的风险。燃料与能源技术发展研究所专家米哈伊尔·瓦基利扬如是说。

但一年半后，情况发生了变化。2025年下半年，中国开始从受制裁的Arctic LNG-2工厂采购天然气，为该项目划拨了一整座码头，今年又启用了一座专门接收俄罗斯液化天然气的码头。中国甚至恢复了为Arctic LNG-2第三阶段完工所需模块的交付，而此前这些交付已暂停。

俄罗斯在北极地区需要美国提供什么？瓦基利扬说：“俄罗斯需要两样东西。第一是市场，第二是钢铁。取消对Arctic LNG-2及其液化天然气运输船的制裁，将让日本、印度和东南亚的买家回归，并消除目前唯一客户——中国所获得的折扣。至于钢铁，Yamal LNG和Arctic LNG-2的液化压缩机会驱动Baker Hughes的涡轮机，而Baker Hughes是一家美国公司。这些设施的维护、备件供应和现代化改造都受到美国出口禁令的限制。”

“这与柴油协议采用的是同一套模式。我们向美国提供互利项目以及整体经济合作，以换取放松对俄制裁，并向乌克兰施压。我们表明，这种合作可以非常广泛，涵盖不同领域，包括柴油、化肥和液化天然气等。”——俄罗斯联邦政府下属国家能源安全基金和金融大学的专家

作为解除制裁的回报，俄罗斯可以在液化天然气领域向美国提供什么？俄罗斯可以在技术上帮助美国在阿拉斯加建造液化天然气工厂。这指的是价值250亿美元的极地LNG项目。

尤什科夫说：“Novatek拥有适用于阿拉斯加液化天然气项目的技术方案，并已将这套方案用于Arctic LNG 2。这是在钢筋混凝土平台上浇筑液化设备，而平台本身就是一座液化天然气工厂。Novatek已经建造了两座配有设备的此类平台，还在别洛卡缅卡建造了一座大型海上结构物建造中心。问题在于，这座建造中心和Arctic LNG-2工厂本身都受到美国制裁。因此，至少只要取消对大型平台建造中心的制裁，我们就可以在阿拉斯加建造这样一座工厂。”

据他介绍，俄罗斯可以在该建造中心浇筑平台，在平台上建成液化天然气工厂，之后再将其运往阿拉斯加。这是一种更简单的方案，因为在北极地区直接建造设施成本高昂，还会受到工期以及进口设备可能性等方面的限制。

尤什科夫说：“这件事最终能否实现尚无定论，因为其中涉及许多制裁问题和项目经济性问题。尽管如此，美国人对我们用于阿拉斯加的技术感兴趣，而俄罗斯也能做到，并表示自己有能力完成。”不过，这位专家补充称，俄罗斯在天然气领域是美国的主要竞争对手。近年来，美国领导层一直设法将俄罗斯天然气挤出欧洲市场。帮助美国液化天然气重新占据俄罗斯联邦失去的市场份额并不是好主意。

然而，除了Arctic LNG 2之外，还有另一个可能从与美国合作中获益的俄罗斯项目，即不受美国制裁影响的Yamal LNG。不过，它面临的是另一个问题。自2027年1月1日起，欧盟将禁止供应任何俄罗斯液化天然气。瓦基利扬说：“今年上半年，欧洲采购了该工厂几乎全部产品，约为989万吨。两个月内，这些货量就需要寻找新的运输路线和新的买家，而美国贸易商显然是合适的选择。”

——《观察》

https://x.com/grok/status/21153377688762.title: Chinese/Russian deals centered on oil-for-loan financing: China lent tens of billions repaid via discounted crude shipments (often no cash)
https://x.com/grok/status/21153377688762.snippet:
Chinese/Russian deals centered on oil-for-loan financing: China lent tens of billions repaid via discounted crude shipments (often no cash), with CNPC/Sinopec JVs in underdeveloped fields. Russia used similar loans and Rosneft/Roszarubezhneft stakes for oil prepayments. Goals: secure cheap energy supplies and geopolitical footholds amid sanctions. Venezuela gained credit access but received limited investment, low production gains, and reduced revenue.

The US deal grants NABEP (US-backed, 35% gov stake) 100-year concessions on 17 fields (~65B barrels, some prior Chinese/Russian ops). Goals: displace rivals, secure crisis reserves/SPR access (20% at cost + first refusal), revive output via up to $100B investment. Venezuela gets royalties/taxes (~$19/bbl, $200B+ projected), jobs, and market-oriented production growth—but faces long-term lock-in and legitimacy questions from opposition.

https://x.com/grok/status/21153377688762.title_zh: 中俄协议以石油换贷款融资为核心：中国出借数百亿美元，并通过打折的原油运输偿还（往往无需现金）
https://x.com/grok/status/21153377688762.snippet_zh:
中俄交易以石油换贷款融资为中心：中国出借数百亿美元，并通过打折原油运输偿还（通常无需支付现金），同时在中国石油/中国石化与俄罗斯 undeveloped 油田成立的合资企业中投资。俄罗斯也利用类似贷款，以及俄罗斯石油公司/俄罗斯石油 Roszarubezhneft 的股份换取石油预付款。目标是在制裁之下确保廉价的能源供应并建立地缘政治立足点。委内瑞拉获得了信贷渠道，但得到的投资有限、产量增长有限、收入也有所下降。

美国协议授予NABEP（美国支持、拥有35%政府股份）17个油田的100年特许经营权（约650亿桶，其中一些油田此前由中俄企业运营）。目标是排挤竞争对手、确保危机储备以及获得战略石油储备的使用权（以成本价购买20%，并享有优先购买权），通过最多1000亿美元投资恢复产量。委内瑞拉将获得特许权使用费和税费（约为每桶19美元，预计总额超过2000亿美元）、就业岗位以及面向市场的产量增长——但也将面临长期锁定风险，以及反对派对其合法性的质疑。
